items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: We were roommates for three years in Tommy Dorsey’s band.

ctx.x: I read some funny story about — did you room with Charlie Shavers for a while?

We were roommates for three years in Tommy Dorsey’s band. There was another giant. Great trumpet player, great arranger, great composer — he wrote “Undecided” and all those wonderful things with the John Kirby small group. I learned a lot rooming with Charlie. He taught me a lot about music, taught me some tap dance steps. Of course when you played the theater in those days, you’d did everything. You’d learn how to be an emcee, you’d learn how to get up and tell some jokes, and do a little shim sham shimmy and a…
Did he used to fall asleep in the tub or something like that?

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Charlie Shavers was in Tommy’s band for three years too. We were roommates.

ctx.x: Do you want to talk about that period?

Charlie Shavers was in Tommy’s band for three years too. We were roommates. There was one of the greatest trumpet players that ever lived. Tommy Dorsey said he was – because he was not only a great trumpet player. He was a great piano player, great arranger, composer. Undecided. He wrote Undecided with the John Kirby Sextet: O’Neill Spencer, brushes . . .
Talk about O’Neill, because a lot of people don’t know about him.
